html:
The Tanimuka, also called Ufaina, are a small Indigenous people of the Colombian Amazon, living along the Mirití-Paraná and Apaporis rivers in southern Colombia. They speak a language of the Tucanoan family, and they share their territory and many customs with the Letuama.

They live in large communal longhouses, the maloca, and farm manioc and coca in forest clearings. Like their neighbours the Karijona, they suffered from the rubber boom of the early 1900s. Today their land lies inside a large Indigenous reserve.
